candidates.explanation: Inferred from the symbol list and knowledge of this boilerplate; the method body was not shown. The reset hash is a stateless JWT. resetPassword only verifies signature and expiry, reads forgotUserId, and sets the new password. Nothing marks the token as used or ties it to the user's current password, so the same link stays valid until it expires and can be replayed.

Signs the reset JWT with only the user id and a global forgot secret. The token has no per-user or one-time component (such as a password-hash fingerprint or stored token id), so it cannot be invalidated once used.
The signing and verification secret is a static config value that does not change after the password changes, so earlier tokens still verify after a successful reset.

fix.description: Make reset tokens single use. Option 1: in forgotPassword, sign the JWT with a per-user secret, e.g. forgotSecret + user.password hash (or password hash + updatedAt). In resetPassword, decode the token to get forgotUserId, load the user, then verifyAsync with the same per-user secret, so the old token fails once the password changes. Option 2: store a hashed one-time token with an expiry, look it up in resetPassword, and delete it when the password is set. Keep deleting the user's sessions after reset.
